stem:
During a storm, Nila sees a bright flash and soon hears thunder. Strong winds in the cloud make water droplets and ice particles rub against each other.

Which sequence correctly produces lightning and thunder?

options.text: Rubbing separates charges; the buildup breaks down the insulating property of air; a sudden discharge is lightning; rapid heating and expansion of air makes thunder.
Thunder is produced first; the sound then separates the charges and forms lightning.
Rubbing separates charges and lightning flashes even when the buildup is too small to break down the insulating property of air.
Only ice particles separate the charges; water droplets play no part in the sequence.

teacher.key_rationale: Friction between droplets and ice separates charges; when the buildup overcomes air's insulating property, discharge is lightning and the heated expanding air makes thunder. Thunder does not come first, and both ice and water droplets take part.
